description: Damage Numbers (core/interface/damage_numbers/damage_numbers.py): how the numbers look and move. Sizes and distances are in the top screen's layout units (400 x 240 at 5:3), times are seconds. The art's cells are in core/interface/damage_numbers/art/damage_numbers_atlas.json.

weak_hitzone.description: A hit whose physical hitzone value (cut, impact or shot, the one the hit used) is at least this shows gold; below it, or unknown, white.

colours.description: The digits' colours (RGBA): a normal hit and the other damage white, a weak spot, blast and the mount's finish gold, a bounce and poison grey.

digit_height.description: A digit's cell (the atlas' 32-pixel row) at size 1x.

frame_seconds.description: The game's frame delta of 1.0 lasts this long (30 frames a second).

pop.description: A new number starts `scale` times its size and settles to it in `seconds`.

rise.description: How far a number rises over its life.

fade_from.description: The part of its life after which a number fades out.

stack.description: A number that lands within `radius` of one younger than `seconds` goes `step` digit cells higher for each, at most `max` of them.

edge.description: How far past the picture's edge (a part of half its side) a number's point may be and still show.

monster_lift.description: A number with no point of its own (poison, blast, the mount, the other damage) shows this many world units over the monster's position.

group.description: The group's layer and draw priority: over the 3D scene and the hunters' names (0), under the target marker (19), every HUD panel (20 and up) and the talk windows (63).

shared_health_species.description: Monster ids whose two parts share one health (Dalamadur and Shah Dalamadur): a part's own health does not drop, so they show no other damage.

styles.description: Per style: `advance`, the step from one digit to the next as a part of a digit's cell width (the outlines overlap); `weak_scale`, how much bigger a weak spot's number is; `effects`, the marks of a critical hit (at most two, drawn in order behind the digits): the atlas' `mark` in `colour` (RGBA), placed at the digits' `anchor` (x: -1 left, 0 centre, 1 right; y: -1 bottom, 0 centre, 1 top) moved by `offset` and sized `size`, both in digit cells, the width growing by the digits' width times `grow`. Wilds: a pink star on its flare at the number's top left, and its white core; Rise: a long red slash across the number, and its bright core; Classic: a straight mark on each side.
